newsitem.title: USA: U.S. urges Japan to do more to open paper market.
newsitem.headline: U.S. urges Japan to do more to open paper market.

text.p: U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky on Monday urged Japan to take steps to open its paper and paperboard markets up to more foreign competition.
"With import penetration far below that of any other industrialized country, access to Japan's paper market remains inadequate," Barshefsky said in a statement.
"We will be working closely with U.S. paper producers to assess in detail the position of foreign paper companies and market access barriers to face in Japan," she said.
The statement outlined the steps USTR plans to take in an effort to open up Japan's paper market as an April 1992 trade agreement between the two countries on the issue expires.

USTR has urged the Japanese government to encourage paper users and distributors to implement open procurement programs for paper and paperboard products which will help guarantee access to foreign supplies.
In the meantime, USTR said it will review Japanese import trends on paper and paperboard and work with the U.S. industry on promoting exports to Japan.
The agency also said it will work with U.S. industry to assess market conditions and trade barriers in the paper and paperboard sector by August 1997.
